parts.label: a
parts.technique: Cumulative distribution F(x) for discrete random variable (summing given probabilities)
parts.reason: S4.1 covers understanding and using simple discrete probability distributions; finding F(3.5) is just summing the given probabilities up to x=3, not a mean/variance calculation, so the S4.1 exclusion (mean and variance of discrete random variables) does not apply here.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Manipulating inequality then summing probabilities from a discrete distribution
parts.reason: Solving 3X-3<X+2 to get X<2.5 and summing P(X=1)+P(X=2) is working with a discrete probability distribution per S4.1, not a mean/variance calculation.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: E(X) for a discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly excludes calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Var(X) for a discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly excludes calculation of variance of discrete random variables; also depends on out-of-spec E(X) from (c).

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Var(aX+b) transformation
parts.reason: Depends on Var(X) from part (d), which is out of spec (excluded by S4.1), so this part only makes sense after an out-of-spec part.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Combining means of two groups to find unknown mean
parts.reason: S2.3 covers measures of central tendency including mean and combining/summary statistics; this is a straightforward mean calculation, not excluded.

parts.label: b

parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly covers calculating standard deviation from summary statistics using Sxx.

parts.technique: Effect of coding (adding constant) on variance

parts.label: c(ii)

parts.reason: S2.3 coding guidance covers effect on mean.

parts.label: c(iii)

parts.reason: S2.3 coding guidance covers effect on standard deviation.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Reasons for using statistical models
parts.reason: General modelling rationale relates to S3.3 (modelling, critiquing assumptions) though not a perfect match; genuinely generic content not tied precisely to a statement.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Calculating Sww (sum of squares) from summary statistics
parts.reason: S2.3 covers use of Sxx-type formula for computing sums of squares from summary statistics; this is the same technique applied to w.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Calculating Std and Sdd (building blocks for correlation/regression)
parts.reason: These quantities are the components used to build the PMCC/regression formulae; S5.1 states 'use of the formula is not required' and S2.2 excludes regression-line calculations, so manually computing Sxy/Sxx equivalents for this purpose is out of spec.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Calculating PMCC using formula/summary statistics
parts.reason: S5.1 explicitly excludes calculation of correlation coefficients via the formula (calculator use only is permitted); this mark scheme requires the formula method using Sdd/Sww etc.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Interpreting PMCC value in context
parts.reason: Although informal interpretation of correlation is in spec (S2.2), this part uses the value of r found in the excluded part (d), so it only makes sense after an out-of-spec part.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Deriving regression line equation from summary statistics
parts.reason: S2.2 explicitly excludes calculations involving regression lines.

parts.label: g
parts.technique: Writing down regression line of d on t via substitution
parts.reason: Depends directly on the excluded regression line derived in (f); also regression-line calculations are excluded by S2.2.

parts.label: h(i)
parts.technique: Using regression equation to estimate a value
parts.reason: Uses the regression equation from (g), which is out of spec (regression line calculations excluded by S2.2).

parts.label: h(ii)
parts.technique: Interpreting gradient of regression line in context
parts.reason: Uses the regression equation from (g)/(f), out of spec per S2.2 exclusion on regression-line calculations.
